# Build and publish the book

## Build locally

Bookdown compiles the `.Rmd` files and CSS into a GitBook-style website. Building the book does not run the computationally intensive IOBRpy workflow.

Install the R packages once:

```r
install.packages(c("bookdown", "rmarkdown", "knitr"))
```

From the repository root:

```bash
Rscript render_book.R
```

The output is written to:

```text
_book/
```

The entry page is:

```text
_book/index.html
```

## Pandoc on Windows

RStudio includes Pandoc, but command-line R may not discover it automatically. In PowerShell:

```powershell
$env:RSTUDIO_PANDOC = "C:\Program Files\RStudio\resources\app\bin\quarto\bin\tools"
& "C:\Program Files\R\R-4.3.3\bin\Rscript.exe" "render_book.R"
```

Replace the R and RStudio paths with the versions installed on your computer.

If R reports:

```text
namespace 'htmltools' ... is already loaded, but >= 0.5.8 is required
```

Install the updated dependency in the project-local library:

```powershell
& "C:\Program Files\R\R-4.3.3\bin\Rscript.exe" -e `
  "dir.create('.r-library', recursive=TRUE, showWarnings=FALSE); install.packages('htmltools', lib='.r-library', repos='https://cloud.r-project.org')"
```

When `.r-library/` exists, `render_book.R` places it first on the R package search path without modifying the system library.

## Preview locally

You can open `_book/index.html` directly. For search and static-resource behavior closer to the deployed site, start a local HTTP server:

```bash
python -m http.server 8000 --directory _book
```

Open:

```text
http://localhost:8000/
```

## GitHub Pages

The repository includes:

```text
.github/workflows/pages.yml
```

Every push to `main` automatically installs the required R packages, renders `_book/`, and deploys the static files to GitHub Pages:

```text
https://hhn0527.github.io/IOBRpy_book/
```

## Update the chapters

Chapter order is defined by `rmd_files` in `_bookdown.yml`. To add a chapter:

1. create a numbered `.Rmd` file in the repository root;
2. add its file name to `rmd_files`;
3. rebuild the book;
4. check navigation, code blocks, internal links, and mobile layout;
5. commit and push the source files.
